goal: reduce the R69-tuned d12 Engram graph-step overhead from +4.5% to <= +3%
result: achieved: 63.69 -> 65.32 ms median over 3 interleaved rounds = +2.56% (pair deltas +2.17/+2.75/+2.56%)
profile_finding: the nano gate kernels themselves are only ~0.65 ms/graph (fwd 0.166 + bwd 0.479 for 2 layers at b=16x1024) and the backward is memory-bound; most of the +2.9 ms was outside the graph: sparse table Adam (~1.4 ms) and redundant grad zeroing (params ~188 MB + engram leaf grads ~100 MB per step, both overwritten by the assignment-based R69 capture).

optimizations.what: use the gate kernel's own output
optimizations.why: native (no-padding) nano path already computes x+gate*value; the wrapper was recomputing it with an extra addcmul kernel
optimizations.impact: removes one elementwise kernel + one write/read of the [16K,4,384] residual per Engram layer

optimizations.what: fused sparse Adam row-update Triton kernel (nanov41/sparse_adam_triton.py)
optimizations.why: torch index_select/gather/index_copy_ + Python loop cost ~0.4 ms/step
optimizations.impact: one kernel per table; row-independent, deterministic

optimizations.what: fused deterministic segment-sum + sparse Adam (one kernel per table)
optimizations.why: collect was ~0.25 ms/table (argsort+unique+segment_reduce+row-grad tensor); the single-record graph path can sum sorted segments and update in one program per unique row
optimizations.impact: removes the intermediate [rows,32] grads tensor and the separate update kernel

optimizations.what: skip param/leaf grad zeroing when accum==1
optimizations.why: R69 captures torch.autograd.grad outputs into baked buffers; replay overwrites every element, so zeroing 188 MB of param grads + ~100 MB leaf grads is dead work (R68 chunked accumulation keeps zeroing)

optimizations.what: int32 stable sort + torch.segment_reduce + single-sync slot assignment
optimizations.why: smaller sort keys and one fewer device->host sync in the fallback collector
128-tile forward, 1 warp/head backward, dynamic v-copy layout, single-warp dldg reduction
optimizations.impact: native 384/640 without padding; the bwd kernel is now bandwidth-bound (0.24 ms/layer), further kernel-only headroom is small

final_measurement.shape: b=16 x seq=1024, graph-only, R69 final_env + accepted flags, 3 interleaved rounds

caveat: R68 chunked-BPTT trainers keep param/leaf zeroing because backward accumulates into the captured grad buffers; the fast sparse path is only used when exactly one captured forward is pending.
